storyNote.name: Apollo 15 Lunar Rover
storyNote.title: Wheels on the Moon
storyNote.description: Imagine driving a car on the Moon! In 1971, the Apollo 15 Lunar Rover made that dream a reality.
storyNote.purpose: Help astronauts travel farther and carry equipment and lunar samples.
storyNote.technology: Battery-powered motors and wire-mesh wheels helped me travel across rough lunar terrain.
achievements: First vehicle driven by humans on the Moon
storyNote.whyLeftBehind: I was parked on the Moon after completing my mission. I was not designed to return to Earth.
storyNote.legacy: I showed how vehicles could help astronauts explore larger areas.
storyNote.question: How would you design a vehicle for the Moon?

storyNote.name: Opportunity
storyNote.title: The Rover That Never Gave Up
storyNote.description: Meet Opportunity! My mission was supposed to last only 90 Martian days, but I explored Mars for almost 15 years.
storyNote.purpose: Search for evidence of ancient water in Martian rocks and soil.
storyNote.technology: I used solar panels, cameras and scientific instruments to study rocks.
achievements: Found evidence of ancient water and potentially habitable environments
storyNote.whyLeftBehind: A massive dust storm in 2018 blocked sunlight from reaching my solar panels. NASA lost contact with me.
storyNote.legacy: My discoveries helped scientists understand the history of Mars.
storyNote.funFact: I traveled farther than a marathon on Mars!
storyNote.question: What other energy source could help a rover survive a dust storm?

storyNote.name: Ingenuity
storyNote.title: A Dream That Learned to Fly
storyNote.description: Meet Ingenuity, the little helicopter that made history by flying on another planet!
storyNote.purpose: Demonstrate powered flight in the thin Martian atmosphere.
storyNote.technology: My lightweight body and fast-spinning rotor blades helped me lift off in the thin atmosphere.
achievements: First powered, controlled flight on another planet
storyNote.whyLeftBehind: My rotor blades were damaged during my final flight in January 2024, preventing further flights.
storyNote.legacy: I opened new possibilities for exploring planets from the sky.
storyNote.funFact: I was designed for five test flights but completed 72!
storyNote.question: How could flying robots help humans explore Mars?
